chunks: What al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn Samāʿah narrated, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalāh, from Dharīḥ, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and informed him of the times of salat (prayer). He said: Perform the fajr prayer when the dawn breaks; perform the first prayer when the sun declines; perform the ʿaṣr prayer after it; perform the maghrib prayer when the disk sets; and perform the ʿatamah prayer when the twilight disappears.

Then Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام came to him the next day and said: Delay fajr until it becomes bright; so he performed it in brightness. Then he delayed ẓuhr until the time in which ʿaṣr had been performed, and ʿaṣr was performed shortly after it; maghrib was performed before the twilight disappeared; and the ʿatamah prayer was performed when a third of the night had passed.

Then he said: What lies between these two times is a time, and the beginning of the time is its most excellent part. Then he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Were it not that I dislike causing hardship to my Ummah, I would have delayed it until the middle of the night.

key_terms.أَوَّلُ الْوَقْتِ: the beginning of the prayer time, described here as most excellent
key_terms.الشَّفَقُ: the twilight glow whose disappearance marks a prayer time
key_terms.الْأُولَى: the first daytime prayer, meaning ẓuhr
key_terms.الْفَجْرَ: the dawn prayer and its time at daybreak
key_terms.مَوَاقِيتَ: the appointed times or prayer times

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about the beginning and ending times of the daily salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith describes how Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام taught the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم the beginning and ending ranges of the daily salat (prayer) times. It establishes that each prayer has a span of valid time between two limits, while also emphasizing that performing the prayer at the beginning of its time is more excellent. It also notes the concession regarding the night prayer, indicating consideration for ease upon the Ummah.
